To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) visual crowding is a result of the brain’s need to sample a limited number of objects in a crowded scene; (2) the brain samples objects based on their similarity; (3) this sampling can occur at any stage in the visual hierarchy, including the level of whole object representations.
1) the visual system uses sparse selection to select a limited set of objects in a scene, and 2) crowding occurs because of this limited selection, rather than degraded visual representations.
